Packet Basin.note: the original harbour: lake packet boats and canal trade, dug 1838 where the east bay is 600 m wide

Fish Basin.note: dug 1871; its outer half was silted and filled in 1971, and the fill is the Fish Flats

Coal Basin.note: dug 1889 beside the Ironworks for the coal trade; the deepest basin

Grain Basin.note: the last basin, 1912, with the grain elevator

crossings.name: Carrick's Ferry
crossings.note: cable ferry at the landing; replaced by the swing bridge

crossings.name: Ferry Street Lift Bridge
crossings.note: swing bridge 1861, rebuilt as a vertical lift 1927; opens for barge tows

crossings.name: Carrick Rail Lift Bridge
crossings.note: the only rail crossing; double-track vertical lift

crossings.name: Carrick Bridge
crossings.note: high-level fixed viaduct built to carry traffic past the lift bridges, which stopped for every ship bound for the western basins

events.text: Carrick's Ferry and the landing: Ferry Street, the Landing Tavern (1796)
Turnpike Avenue cut toward the north-west
Packet Basin dug in the east bay, where the river is 700 m wide and slow; Dock Road leads to it; the Old Town grid grows east of the landing
Swing bridge replaces the ferry; South Line reaches the south bank (rail car float)
Ironworks mills and the company grid
Fish Basin dug in the west bay
Coal Basin dug in the west bay, beside the Ironworks; Coal Spur
Rail Lift Bridge and the North Line; Packet Spur follows in 1894
Grain Basin dug in the east bay
Ferry Street swing bridge rebuilt as a lift
The great flood: the river reaches 222 m
Floodwall and pump stations built (protects x = -3,000..+3,000 m, all four basins); the far ends of the bays are left to the river
Northgate built out on the platted heights
Carrick Bridge opens: a high-level viaduct carrying traffic past the lift bridges, which stop for every ship bound for the west bay
The outer end of Fish Basin silted and filled: the Fish Flats

landmarks.name: The Landing Tavern
landmarks.note: oldest surviving building; the ferry landing's inn

landmarks.name: Kilbride Precinct (south-bank police)
landmarks.note: the south bank's own station: the viaduct can close

landmarks.name: Carrick Waterworks and River Intake
landmarks.note: intake at the western (upstream) end, above every outfall

landmarks.name: Carrick Bridge (datum)
landmarks.note: origin of the local lat/lon frame

sites.name: Bridge Street eviction
sites.notes: The inherited file. Occupants have organised and the coalition is watching.

sites.name: Civic Plaza rally
sites.notes: Campaign events land here as the election nears. Rarely erupts; catastrophic if it does.

sites.name: Council hearing protest
sites.notes: Budget hearings draw both unions and tenants.

sites.name: Veterans Bridge march
sites.notes: Marches cross here toward the plaza. The bridge is a chokepoint.

sites.name: Front Street flat
sites.notes: Fraud warrant on a downtown apartment. Daylight, witnesses, phones.

sites.name: Mill No. 3 squat
sites.notes: Gang using the closed mill. Long sightlines, catwalks, no witnesses.

sites.name: Foundry Row warrant
sites.notes: Narrow two-storey rowhouse on Foundry Road.

sites.name: Brass Rail tavern
sites.notes: Barricaded suspect behind the bar. Regulars still inside.

sites.name: Yard office hostage
sites.notes: Hostage in the dispatcher's office. Standing trains block two approaches.

sites.name: Riverside Homes block
sites.notes: Gang house in a occupied building; families in adjacent units.

sites.name: Floodwall tool shed
sites.notes: Isolated, low visibility, one door.

sites.name: Ebenezer hall meeting
sites.notes: Coalition meeting. Officers present are noticed.

sites.name: Bluff Road bungalow
sites.notes: Domestic barricade on the bluff. Neighbours are police families.

sites.name: St. Brendan's hall memorial
sites.notes: Memorial gathering. Union attention.

sites.name: Holy Cross funeral
sites.notes: Officer funeral procession. Press at the gate.

sites.name: Kilbride Avenue corner store
sites.notes: Hostage taken during a robbery. Houses on both sides.

sites.name: Warehouse Row unit 7
sites.notes: Stash house in a loading-dock unit.

sites.name: Hale Armour records warrant
sites.notes: Politically loaded. Kettering's ticket will react either way.

sites.name: Container stack standoff
sites.notes: Barricaded among stacked containers. Cover everywhere, sightlines nowhere.

sites.name: Grain elevator hostage
sites.notes: Vertical building: stairs, catwalks, a long fall.

sites.name: Wharf Street flat
sites.notes: Hostage in a flat beside the rail line.

sites.name: Heights Boulevard villa
sites.notes: Financial-crimes warrant at a wealthy address. Lawyers arrive first.

sites.name: Harlan Park concert
sites.notes: Large outdoor event. Many families, few exits.

sites.name: Channel 6 lobby occupation
sites.notes: Occupation of a TV station. Live cameras are already inside.

sites.name: Harlan Avenue bungalow
sites.notes: Domestic barricade on a residential street.

one river spans the full east-west extent
river is narrowest at the bridge and widens steadily east and west (>= 3x centre width by x = +-3,250; symmetric)
four harbour basins, one per quadrant, each open to the river with >= 2 finger piers that stop >= 40 m short of the bank
the harbour is in the wide reaches, not at the narrows: every basin is >= 1800 m from the bridge and sits where the river is >= 600 m wide (>= 1.8x its width at the bridge)
the basins are not mirror images: four distinct size/pier signatures
exactly one MAJOR crossing (the 62 m viaduct, >= 2.5x the lanes of all minor spans combined); every crossing sits where the river is <= 400 m wide; nothing else crosses the water
crossings are redundant but not free: closing both leaves two disconnected banks; closing either one alone leaves the banks joined
six wards partition the extent (no gaps, no overlaps)
every street's declared ward contains its midpoint
the city limit lies inside the extent and contains the bridge
no street carriageway lies in water
the street network (with the lift bridge) is one connected component (>= 99.5% of length); without the lift bridge it is exactly two, one per bank
